title: Compatibility with finite reduction
statement: In the six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism, let $1\le m\le n$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_{E,n})$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. Write $K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ and $L_m=L\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ for their finite reductions. Then the square comparing $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ through the finite-reduction compatibilities of $Rf_!$, $-\otimes^L$ and $Lf^*$ commutes; hence $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ is.

proof.text: First check the coefficient domains, without invoking axioms (A3) or (A5) of the datum. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose bounded constructible étale representatives of $K,L$ and retain their comparison isomorphisms as étale-origin witnesses. By clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], the representatives have the same finite Tor amplitudes. The constructible variant of [lem-sf-flat-model] applies because $X,Y$ are finite type over a field, hence Noetherian: choose bounded flat constructible étale models $P,Q$. With $A=A_{E,n}$ and $B=A_{E,m}$, their termwise tensors with $B$ represent the derived reductions. Each term remains flat over $B$, since $(P^i\otimes_A B)\otimes_B N=P^i\otimes_A N$ for a $B$-module sheaf $N$ and restriction of scalars is exact; it remains constructible since on a common finite stratification its values are finite modules tensored with the finite ring $B$. Thus the reductions are bounded constructible and have finite Tor amplitude, with the same bounds. The same models show that $K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude: inverse image is exact for constant coefficients, takes each flat locally constant term on a stratum to such a term on its inverse image, and the bounded total tensor model has amplitude bounded by the sums of the two intervals. Clause (i) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] returns these objects and their finite-Tor properties to the pro-étale site. All operations below are taken on these witnessed realizations.

Put $\rho_T=-\otimes_A^L B$ on each scheme $T$, and suppress the subscript when its scheme is determined. Let $c_f(M):\rho Rf_{!,A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}\rho M$ be [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], and let $s$ and $t$ denote the tensor and pullback comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Define $u$ by $\rho(Rf_{!,A}K\otimes_A^L L)\xrightarrow{s}\rho Rf_{!,A}K\otimes_B^L L_m\xrightarrow{c_f(K)\otimes1}Rf_{!,B}K_m\otimes_B^L L_m$. Define $v$ by $\rho Rf_{!,A}(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)\xrightarrow{c_f(K\otimes Lf_A^*L)}Rf_{!,B}\rho(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)\xrightarrow{Rf_{!,B}(s,t)}Rf_{!,B}(K_m\otimes_B^L Lf_B^*L_m)$. Both $u$ and $v$ are isomorphisms by the cited statements and the domains checked in step 1. The square to be proved is precisely
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\rho(Rf_{!,A}K\otimes_A^L L)&\xrightarrow{\rho(\operatorname{PF}_{A})}&\rho Rf_{!,A}(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)\\
{\scriptstyle u}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle v}\\
Rf_{!,B}K_m\otimes_B^L L_m&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{B}}&Rf_{!,B}(K_m\otimes_B^L Lf_B^*L_m).
\end{array}
$$
In particular its upper arrow is the reduction of the level-$n$ map.

The scheme $Y$ is finite type over $k$, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification $f=pj$. Put $M=j_!K$. Before applying coefficient comparison to $p$, check its input domain: by exactness of $j_!$ in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], $M$ is bounded, and extending a finite constructible stratification of $K$ by the closed complement, on which extension by zero is zero, shows that $M$ is constructible. For a sheaf $N$ of $A$-modules on $\overline X$, [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] gives $M\otimes_A^L N\cong j_!(K\otimes_A^L j^{-1}N)$; exactness of $j_!$ therefore gives the same Tor interval as $K$. The tensor argument of step 1 gives the finite-Tor domain for $M\otimes_A^L Lp_A^*L$ as well. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], these bounded constructible objects admit the required étale-origin witnesses. Thus the proper-factor coefficient comparisons below are applied on their stated domains. The definition [def-exchange-projection], with the notation [def-sf-pf], writes $\operatorname{PF}_{A}=Rp_{*,A}(\gamma_A)\circ\pi_A$, where $\gamma_A:j_!K\otimes_A^L Lp_A^*L\to j_!(K\otimes_A^L Lf_A^*L)$ is the specified open-immersion tensor isomorphism and $\pi_A$ is the transpose of $(\varepsilon_A\otimes1)\circ\mu_A$. To check the proper direct-image part, write $F_A=Lp_A^*$, $G_A=Rp_{*,A}$, and likewise at $B$, and orient the pullback comparison as $t:F_B\rho\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho F_A$. Write $c_M:\rho G_A M\to G_B\rho M$ for the coefficient comparison; for proper $p$, use the compactification $(\operatorname{id},p)$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], so this is the compact-support comparison. Its counit compatibility in [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] and [lem-fix-operation-reduction] is the typed identity
$$
\varepsilon_{B,\rho M}\circ F_B(c_M)=\rho(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ t_{G_AM}.
$$
After identifying the tensor and pullback targets, the transpose under $F_B\dashv G_B$ of each route in the direct-image comparison square is the following single composite:
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_B\rho(G_AM\otimes_A^L L)
&\xrightarrow{t}\rho F_A(G_AM\otimes_A^L L)
\xrightarrow{\rho\mu_A}\rho(F_AG_AM\otimes_A^L F_AL)\\
&\xrightarrow{\rho(\varepsilon_A\otimes1)}\rho(M\otimes_A^L F_AL)
\xrightarrow{s}\rho M\otimes_B^L\rho F_AL
\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_L^{-1}}\rho M\otimes_B^L F_B\rho L.
\end{aligned}
$$
For the route through $\rho\pi_A$, this follows by its defining transpose and the displayed counit identity for the target comparison. For the route through $\pi_B$, substitute the displayed identity for $\varepsilon_B\circ F_Bc_M$; coherence of $s,t,\mu$ gives exactly the written composite. The required coherence and preservation of the units and counits are explicit clauses of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Adjunction therefore equates these two routes. For the open-immersion factor, write $d_H:\rho j_{!,A}H\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}\rho H$, the compact-support comparison for $j$ (its compactification is $(j,\operatorname{id})$). Reduction of the specified open tensor map satisfies
$$
d_{K\otimes Lf_A^*L}\circ\rho\gamma_A
=\gamma_B\circ(d_K\otimes1)
$$
after inserting $s,t$ on the source and target. Indeed $\gamma$ is the open tensor identification of [def-exchange-projection], built from the tensor comparison and the extension-by-zero adjunction; reducing each tensor, unit and counit arrow gives the corresponding $B$-arrow by [lem-fix-operation-reduction], in the same order. Thus the two sides are the same composite, including the pullback-composition identification $Lj^*Lp^*=Lf^*$. Composing this identity with the direct-image identity proves $v\circ\rho(\operatorname{PF}_A)=\operatorname{PF}_B\circ u$, as required. As required by the warning in [lem-sf-generating-class-determination], this equality of natural transformations has been checked from the constructions; no equality is inferred merely from values on generators.

The commutative square and the inverses of $u,v$ show that $\rho(\operatorname{PF}_A)$ is invertible if and only if $\operatorname{PF}_B$ is invertible. This cancellation concerns the reduced map. For the asserted equivalence with the original map, apply [thm-sf-pf-finite] at $A$ and $B$ to the étale representatives from step 1: both $\operatorname{PF}_A$ and $\operatorname{PF}_B$ are isomorphisms, so the claimed equivalence holds. For the pro-étale realizations use the witnessed-realization clause of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], which states precisely the same invertibility there. The representatives satisfy its bounded constructibility and finite-Tor hypotheses by step 1. This completes both the commutativity and the original-map invertibility assertion.
